text:
anya: ran into a subtle hang in the Go generator sample when cancelling during token refresh/handshake. reproducible locally, attaching a tiny harness in the gist: https://internal.gists/redwood/go-gen-hang-3805

dmitri: thanks. quick symptoms? stack traces?

anya: minimal: call `Generate.Subscribe(ctx)` -> handshake starts -> token refresher pushes new creds -> user cancels ctx -> caller returns but two goroutines remain blocked: one trying to write to authCh, another reading response. stacks point to `auth/refresher.go:notify` and `stream/reader.go:run`.

felix: classic channel-block on send with nobody receiving. refresher should select on ctx.Done() when notifying. simple fix:
```diff
- authCh <- token
+ select {
+ case authCh <- token:
+ case <-ctx.Done():
+   return ctx.Err()
+ }
```

anya: that patch fixes the immediate leak in my harness, but it surfaced a larger UX/ergonomics issue: our public `Subscribe` returns a channel and the library spawns goroutines for users, which makes cancellation ownership ambiguous. newcomers keep forgetting to Close or wire ctx properly.

dmitri: what are you proposing?

anya: prototype a pull-style API: `client.Pull(ctx, req) (Stream, error)` where Stream exposes `Recv(ctx)` and `Close()`. Pattern is explicit: callers pass ctx into Recv and are responsible for Close. Example we drafted:
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 2*time.Second)
defer cancel()
stream, err := client.Pull(ctx, req)
if err != nil { return err }
defer stream.Close()
for {
  chunk, err := stream.Recv(ctx)
  if err != nil { break }
  // process chunk
}
```

felix: that maps nicely to Go idioms (io.Reader-ish) and makes cancel semantics obvious. We can implement `Subscribe` as a compatibility shim that adapts the Pull API to the old channel style while wiring ctx/Close correctly and emitting a deprecation log.

docs-bot: note: update `docs/sdk/go/streaming.md` with migration path and example. Also include parity note: Python/TS currently close net.Conn on cancel which unwinds goroutines; Go will prefer explicit Close/Recv semantics.

qa-bot: please add a unit test `TestCancelDuringHandshake_noGoroutineLeak` that counts goroutines before/after and asserts no leak. include harness to simulate delayed auth refresh. CI link: https://ci.internal/streams/3805 (failing on master).

dmitri: good. also add a small shim in the adapter so that existing users using `Subscribe()` don't break. The shim will spawn a goroutine to forward Recv -> user channel but ensure reads respect ctx and call Close on exit. Emit a one-time log warning: "Subscribe() is deprecated, use Pull()."

anya: I've got a branch with both fixes: select-on-ctx for refresher + the Pull prototype + shim + unit test. Master leaks ~3 goroutines per cancel; branch shows zero. I'll open an RFC describing the API, migration guide, sample update under `sdk/go/examples/generator-pull`, and a CLI demo.

felix: perf note: Recv(ctx) has an extra ctx check per chunk; add `BenchmarkStreamRecv` to confirm overhead is negligible. If overhead shows up at very high QPS we can optimize by minimizing context allocations.

docs-bot: add docs checklist: examples, changelog entry, Dedicated migration note (some enterprise users embed the client deeply), and a short section comparing unregistering vs Close semantics across SDKs.

qa-bot: once RFC/PR is up I'll run the goroutine-leak stress test on the infra matrix (linux/amd64, linux/arm64) and add the test to CI gate.

anya: thanks. opening PR+RFC now. tagging @dmitri @felix @qa-bot for review. :thumbsup:
